title: Operational Coding Theorem for the AWGN Channel — Random Gaussian Codebooks and the Sphere-Packing Converse

problemStatement.formal: For the AWGN channel $Y = X + Z$ with $Z \sim N(0,N)$ and power constraint $\frac{1}{n}\sum_i \mathbb{E}[X_i^2] \le P$, the operational capacity equals the information capacity $C(P,N) = \tfrac12\log(1+P/N)$: (achievability) if $R < C$ then random Gaussian codebooks with joint-typicality decoding give $P_e^{(n)} \to 0$; (converse) if $R > C$ then $P_e^{(n)} \not\to 0$, via Fano's inequality and the sphere-packing bound $2^{nR} \le (\tfrac{P+N}{N})^{n/2}$.
problemStatement.plain: The parent proof pins down the value of the AWGN capacity, C = (1/2)log(1+P/N). This problem asks to connect that number to actual communication: prove achievability (random Gaussian codebooks decode almost perfectly for rates below C, so a good code exists) and the converse (no code can beat C, because each transmitted point is blurred by noise into a small ball and only so many disjoint balls fit in the output region).
whyMatters: Shannon's capacity is only a number until the coding theorem ties it to achievable operational rates.
The random-coding achievability and sphere-packing/Fano converse are the theorems practitioners actually cite; turbo, LDPC, and polar codes are benchmarked against this operational limit.
Formalizing it forces reusable Lean infrastructure: continuous jointly-typical sets, the AEP, Fano's inequality, and Gaussian-norm concentration.

proven: AWGN capacity value C(P,N) = (1/2)log(1+P/N) as an entropy difference (shannon-channel-coding-awgn, awgn_capacity_achieved and awgn_capacity_upper_bound).
Gaussian differential entropy h(N(mu,sigma^2)) = (1/2)log(2 pi e sigma^2) and the Gaussian max-entropy property at fixed variance (shannon-entropy-oq-01).
Discrete channel coding theorems for BSC and BEC as finite-alphabet templates (shannon-channel-coding-oq-02, shannon-channel-coding-bec).
open: Continuous-alphabet mutual information I(X;Y) and the identity I(X;Y) = h(Y) - h(Z) are prose-only in the parent.
The variance-of-a-sum relation E[Y^2] = P + N appears only as the converse hypothesis, not as a derived fact.
No Lean formalization of continuous jointly-typical sets, the random-coding error exponent, or Fano's inequality for continuous channels.
knownResults.goal: Formalize the operational coding theorem in two pieces: (1) achievability via random Gaussian codebooks and joint-typicality decoding with expected error to 0 for R < C, and (2) the converse via Fano plus the sphere-packing volume bound. A tractable first milestone is the geometric sphere-packing cardinality bound 2^{nR} <= ((P+N)/N)^{n/2}.
